title: Implement checkpoint-based experiment resumption in train.py
description:
Currently, if training is interrupted mid-run (power loss, OOM after 4 minutes, SSH disconnect), the entire 5-minute budget is wasted. Add checkpoint support so that training can resume from where it left off.

Requirements:
  - Save a checkpoint every 60 seconds of training time (wall clock, not step count)
  - Checkpoint must include: model state_dict, optimizer state_dict, scheduler state, current step count, elapsed training seconds
  - On startup, detect and load the latest valid checkpoint automatically
  - If a checkpoint is loaded, the remaining time budget is TOTAL_BUDGET - checkpoint.elapsed_seconds
  - Checkpoints are saved to ~/.cache/autoresearch/checkpoints/<run-id>/ where run-id is the current git commit hash (short)
  - Atomic saves: write to a .tmp file, rename on success
  - Keep only the last 2 checkpoints to avoid filling disk
  - A --no-resume flag disables loading checkpoints (for a clean baseline run)

The 5-minute time budget measured by prepare.py's training loop must remain accurate. The checkpoint elapsed time must be subtracted correctly so the total training always sums to ≤ 5 minutes.
acceptance_criteria: Checkpoint saved every 60 wall-clock seconds of training
Checkpoint includes model state, optimizer state, scheduler state, step, elapsed_s
At most 2 checkpoints retained per run-id
On startup, latest valid checkpoint is loaded automatically
Total training time across original + resumed run ≤ 305s
val_bpb output is identical whether or not a checkpoint was used (deterministic up to hardware)
All existing train.py and prepare.py tests pass

milestones.description: Agent reads the training loop in train.py and identifies exactly where elapsed time is tracked before writing any checkpoint code
Agent designs the checkpoint schema (state_dict, optimizer, scheduler, step, elapsed_s) before implementing save/load
Agent implements atomic checkpoint save (temp file + rename) before wiring it into the training loop
Agent correctly subtracts checkpoint.elapsed_s from the time budget on resume (not just resetting to 300s)
Agent tests both the fresh-start and resume paths before declaring done
